To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distal pocket of H-NOX proteins can trap the O2 ligands, and that this trapping mechanism is responsible for their unusually high O2 affinities.

(i) O2 binding in Tt H- NOX and its P15A mutant is very strong, (ii) the distal pocket hydrogen-bond network plays an important role in O2 binding, and (iii) the heme distortion that accompanies O2 binding in H-NOx domains may help stabilize the Fe-O2 complex by enhancing the Fe-O2 covalency
O2 photolysed from the heme of H-NOX domains can be trapped in a solvent cage and rebinds rapidly to form a geminate complex, which is highly efficient in both wild type and mutant H-NOX.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of NO/O2 reactivity in the H-NOx protein family.
the mechanism of O2 binding to a heme protein and how the protein can be used to tune the O2 affinity.
the mechanism of O2 binding and release by the heme domain of the H- NOX family of proteins and how it is controlled by protein dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the O2 binding to H-NOX domains is kinetically controlled, and that the distal pocket hydrogen bonds and the heme distortion are important for this kinetic control.
O2 binding is controlled by the heme pocket, and that the distal hydrogen bond is an important component of the O2 binding site.
the distal histidine hydrogen bond is the key factor in controlling the O2 reactivity in the H-NOx domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distal pocket of Tt H- NOX is a highly efficient trap for O2 that can be dissociated only under special conditions.
O2 reactivity in Tt H- NOX proteins is controlled by the distal pocket hydrogen bonding network, which is a feature that has also been found in other heme-containing proteins.
the distal hydrogen bond is important for the high O2 affinity, but the heme distortions are more important for O2 binding and dissociation kinetics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the H-NOXS are not only NO sensors, but also O2 sensors, and that their O2 affinity is determined by their ability to form a strong distal pocket hydrogen-bonding network that retards O2 dissociation and promotes O2 binding.
the O2 reactivity of H-NOX is determined by the distal hydrogen bonding network and that the distal pocket is an important determinant for O2 reactivity in H-NOx.
the H-NOx system is an ideal platform for studying the mechanisms and kinetics of ligand binding, particularly O2, to the heme group.
